content.title: About
content.content: Kashi Chewy is a whole‑grain granola bar that combines whole grains, nuts, and dried fruit. The bar has a soft, chewy texture and a mildly sweet flavor thanks to natural sweeteners like honey and maple syrup.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Kashi brand was founded in 1981 and is known for its whole‑grain products.
Kashi Chewy bars contain no artificial colors or flavors.
Typical ingredients include oat flakes, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, and dried cranberries.
The bar is marketed as a source of plant protein and fiber.
Packaging is usually made from recyclable material.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Protein from nuts and seeds aids tissue repair and supports muscle mass.

items.title: Contains whole grains
items.content: Whole grains provide slow‑release energy and help stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Nuts and seeds supply monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Natural antioxidants
items.content: Dried fruits such as cranberries contain polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Nut and seed allergy
items.content: The bar may contain sunflower, pumpkin seeds, and other allergens that can trigger reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although sweetened naturally, the bar still contains a notable amount of sugar, which may be a concern for diabetics.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: One bar can provide 180–210 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Oat flakes may contain gluten, important for individuals with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is convenient as a snack between meals, can be chopped into yogurt or oatmeal, or used as a sweet addition to smoothies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in the original wrapper or an airtight container. For extended shelf life, keep refrigerated to maintain texture.
